Usage: las agent friends [OPTIONS] [NAME]

  An agent's las-friends — the agents it is linked to — show, add or remove.

    las agent friends                    # the friends of the agent in the cwd
    las agent friends --add Vortexia     # link one (it is mutual when Vortexia links back)
    las agent friends --remove Vortexia  # unlink it (only this side)
    las agent friends --add coach@uy-mac # another Mac: Name@env, over vortex-relay
    las agent send --to Monkey --friends "¿en qué andan?"   # message all of them

  Stored as `friends` in the agent's .las-agent.json; the widget's children
  drawer shows them (list and panel tabs) next to its sessions.

Options:
  --add TEXT     Link this agent (repeatable).
  --remove TEXT  Unlink this agent (repeatable).
  --help         Show this message and exit.

Usage: las agent send [OPTIONS] MESSAGE

  Generic send: point-to-point (--to) or scope broadcast (--scope), local or
  cross-machine.

  Replaces `inject`'s exact-name-only, single-machine model with one primitive
  that also reaches another environment (a different Mac, via vortex-relay —
  see vortexia/docs/vortex-relay-poc.md):

    las agent send --to System "..."            # local, or vortex-relayed if not found locally
    las agent send --to "System@uy-mac" "..."    # explicit, disambiguates a name collision
    las agent send --scope "facturacion, pagos" "..."   # broadcast; 0, 1, or several may reply
    las agent send --to RelayRobotics --children "..."  # every subordinate of RelayRobotics (see `las agent children`)
    las agent send --to Monkey --friends "..."           # every las-friend of Monkey (see `las agent friends`)
    las agent send --to Robo --session shell "ls -la"    # one connected session of Robo (see `las agent sessions`)
    las agent send --to Robo --all-sessions "heads up"   # every connected session of Robo
    las agent send --to Robo --session shell --cc "make test"   # the shell runs it (after y/N), Robo's Claude gets a cc

  With no --session/--all-sessions the recipient's own choice applies (`las
  agent target`): its last-used session, all of them, or one.

  `inject` still works unchanged for existing scripts/skills — this is the new
  generic entry point going forward, not a replacement in place.

Options:
  --to TEXT       Exact agent name, optionally "Name@env" for a specific
                  environment (cross-machine)
  --scope TEXT    Free-text scope/intent instead of an exact name — broadcasts
                  to whoever matches, possibly more than one agent
  --from TEXT     Sender name shown to the recipient(s)
  --children      Deliver to every subordinate of --to (agents whose folder
                  sits under its folder) instead of to --to itself
  --deep          With --children: the whole subtree, not only direct
                  subordinates
  --friends       Deliver to every las-friend of --to (the `friends` list in
                  its .las-agent.json) instead of to --to itself
